question: What completes the rolled-shell gesture and what ritual fault can occur during drinking?
premises: When the two hands are bound without gaps, the formation is called the rolled shell.
During the time of drinking, drops may fall from that formation.
Drops that fall to the earth indicate an imperfect performance.
inference: The rolled-shell gesture must be tightly sealed, because any drops falling to the ground during drinking mark a ritual defect.
uncertainties: The verse states the consequence implicitly; the remedial action is not specified here.
plain_english: When the two hands are bound without any gap, that is called the rolled shell; but if, at the time of drinking, drops fall to the ground, the gesture has not been properly formed.
